comment: One row for each core rule of the heap proof (src/fort/ownership_heap.ft).
The heap module is not part of the compiler binary: its tests compile it from source.
So the build compiles the case-group test, and that test binary is the measured binary.
The stages run the case groups, the provenance test, then the other ten heap test programs.
Run it on a darwin host with --runner 'bash -c' after cmake --preset debug,
or in the Linux VM with the default runner. ZERO_AR_DATE=1 keeps the darwin md5 stable.
Each stage runs from test/fort, where the tests write their sandbox directories.
The md5 of a compiler does not change for a mutant. The md5 of the test program does.
The rows toolchain-4.2-witness and toolchain-4.2-exit-witness left the table when the
proof dropped its witness: the code that they mutated is gone, and a separate checker
validates the candidates. The four toolchain-4.2-candidate rows hold the candidate events.
